newsitem.title: USA: Producer prices jump 0.5 percent in December.
newsitem.headline: Producer prices jump 0.5 percent in December.

text.p: Prices at the wholesale level posted their biggest increase all year in December, the government said Thursday, as surging energy prices offset an otherwise calm inflation report.
The Labour Department said the Producer Price Index advanced 0.5 percent last month, after rising 0.4 percent in November.
The December increase was the biggest since December 1995's gain of 0.6 percent.
However, excluding food and energy prices, the "core" rate of inflation rose by only 0.1 percent in December, matching November's rise.
Wall Street economists had forecast a 0.3 percent increase in wholesale prices overall and a 0.1 percent rise in the core rate.

The inflation-sensitive 30-year U.S. Treasury bond gained a quarter of a point after the report was issued, and its yield, which moves in the opposite direction of its price, slipped to 6.82 percent from 6.84 percent late Wednesday.
"It's actually good news, bad news: good news in terms of the core, bad new in terms of the energy story," said Mike Niemira, an economist at the Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi.

"It was all energy prices,' added Astrid Adolfson, of MCM Moneywatch Inc. "But it was expected that food (prices) would fall more and they didn't, so that is why the overall was up 0.5 percent, higher than expected."
For all of 1996, producer prices were up 2.8 percent. But excluding the volatile food and energy components, prices rose by only 0.6 percent last year.

Energy prices rose 3.1 percent in December, the biggest monthly increase since December 1995's 3.8 percent gain. Residential natural gas prices climbed 1.7 percent after rising a record 3.8 percent in November. Gasoline prices surged 5.2 percent in December while heating oil prices rose 4.9 percent.

But food prices fell 0.1 percent last month, matching November's drop. Passenger car prices rose 0.3 percent in December following a gain of 0.5 percent in November. Tobacco prices rose 0.3 percent after rising 0.1 percent in November.
In December, prices of intermediate goods -- those that require further processing -- rose 0.4 percent after gaining 0.2 percent in the previous month.
Prices of crude goods jumped 4.2 percent after rising 1.8 percent in November.
In another report, the department said first-time jobless claims fell 13,000 to 361,000 in the week ended Jan. 4 from a revised 374,000 the prior week.
The less volatile four-week moving average rose to 357,250 from 354,500.
